basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Binds release identity to the build run, its artifacts and attestations, unlike a version tag in source control.
Differs from a deployment, which puts a release into a runtime environment.
Carries lifecycle and support declarations, such as end of support or withdrawal.
References SBOMs and test evidence by link instead of containing them.

may: Assign release identity and record build provenance.
Bind artifacts with digests to the release.
Record reproducibility checks and their outcome.
Publish release notes and change communication drafts for review.
mustNot: Promote a release to published or supported state without authorization.
Publish artifacts whose digests do not match the recorded build.
Sign a release with a key it was not issued for.
Rewrite or delete a published release instead of withdrawing or superseding it.
Omit known security issues from release notes.
requiresHuman: Withdrawing a release for security or legal reasons.

considerations: Users depend on accurate release notes to judge the risk of upgrading.
Withdrawn or vulnerable releases left available can harm users who cannot tell the difference.
End of support affects people who cannot afford to upgrade quickly.
affectedParties: Users and operators of the software

items: A release record has a version, artifacts with digests, build provenance and a lifecycle state.
Often confused with a source tag, a build run and a deployment.
Tampered build pipelines produce malicious but signed releases.
Ambiguous version identity leads users to install the wrong artifact.
Unannounced breaking changes cause outages downstream.
SLSA build provenance and in-toto attestations.
NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework.
Sigstore signing and transparency log practice.
